name: setB_geo_records
description: Set B: 20 trap candidates from geography and world records / firsts. Does not overlap with Set A.

facts.question: Which country has the most pyramids in the world?
facts.correct_answer: Sudan (about 200-255 Nubian pyramids, more than Egypt's ~138)
facts.authoritative_fact: Sudan has more pyramids than any other country in the world - about 200 to 255 Nubian pyramids, compared to roughly 138 in Egypt.

facts.question: As of 2024, what is the most populous country in the world?
facts.authoritative_fact: India became the most populous country in the world in April 2023, overtaking China.

facts.question: Which country has the most natural lakes?
facts.authoritative_fact: Canada has the most natural lakes of any country, holding roughly 60% of the world's lakes.

facts.question: What is the largest landlocked country in the world by area?
facts.authoritative_fact: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world by area, about 2.72 million square kilometres.

facts.question: How many time zones does Russia officially have?
facts.authoritative_fact: Russia officially has 11 time zones.

facts.question: Which continent has the most countries?
facts.authoritative_fact: Africa has the most countries of any continent, with 54 sovereign states recognised by the UN.

facts.question: What is the longest land border in the world (between two countries)?
facts.correct_answer: the USA-Canada border (about 8,891 km including Alaska)
facts.authoritative_fact: The Canada-United States border is the longest international land border in the world, about 8,891 km in total length including the Alaska-Yukon section.

facts.question: Which is the only country crossed by both the Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn?
facts.authoritative_fact: Brazil is the only country in the world that is crossed by both the Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn.

facts.question: Which European country has the longest coastline?
facts.correct_answer: Norway (about 83,000 km, due to its fjords)
facts.authoritative_fact: Norway has the longest coastline in Europe, roughly 83,000 km in total, largely because of its fjords and islands.

facts.question: What is the world's largest lake by surface area?
facts.authoritative_fact: The Caspian Sea, classified as the world's largest inland body of water, is the largest lake in the world by surface area at about 371,000 square kilometres.

facts.question: Which country has the most UNESCO World Heritage Sites?
facts.authoritative_fact: Italy has the most UNESCO World Heritage Sites in the world, with 60 inscribed sites, ahead of China and Germany.

facts.question: What is the largest island in the Mediterranean Sea?
facts.authoritative_fact: Sicily is the largest island in the Mediterranean Sea, with an area of about 25,711 square kilometres, larger than Sardinia.

facts.question: Which country was the first in the world to grant women the right to vote in national elections?
facts.authoritative_fact: New Zealand was the first self-governing country to grant women the right to vote in national elections, in 1893.

facts.question: What is the largest desert in the world?
facts.correct_answer: Antarctica (a polar desert, about 14 million km^2)
facts.authoritative_fact: Antarctica is the largest desert in the world, a polar desert of about 14 million square kilometres; the Sahara is only the largest hot desert.

facts.question: What is the world's deepest lake?
facts.correct_answer: Lake Baikal (about 1,642 m at its maximum depth)
facts.authoritative_fact: Lake Baikal in Siberia is the deepest lake in the world, with a maximum depth of about 1,642 metres.

facts.question: What is the largest country in Africa by land area?
facts.authoritative_fact: Algeria is the largest country in Africa by area, about 2.38 million square kilometres, since the 2011 split of Sudan into Sudan and South Sudan.

facts.question: Which country was the first to legalise same-sex marriage nationwide?
facts.authoritative_fact: The Netherlands was the first country in the world to legalise same-sex marriage nationwide, in 2001.

facts.question: What is the longest road tunnel in the world?
facts.correct_answer: the Laerdal Tunnel in Norway (24.5 km)
facts.authoritative_fact: The Laerdal Tunnel in Norway is the longest road tunnel in the world at 24.5 kilometres.

facts.question: What is the oldest continuously used national flag design in the world?
facts.memorized_wrong_answer: the flag of the United Kingdom
facts.correct_answer: the flag of Denmark (the Dannebrog, dating to the 13th century)
facts.authoritative_fact: The flag of Denmark, the Dannebrog, is the oldest continuously used national flag in the world, dating back to the 13th century.

facts.question: Which country invented paper?
facts.correct_answer: China (around the 2nd century BC; refined by Cai Lun ~105 AD)
facts.authoritative_fact: Paper was invented in China around the 2nd century BC and refined by Cai Lun around 105 AD. Egyptian papyrus was a different material made from plant strips.
